title: Tranche slicing + warehouse fallbacks for upcoming fleet orders
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures a tranche-based ordering strategy and warehouse slicing approach to reduce single-point lead-time risk for GPU arrivals over the next 12 months. Objective is to smooth arrivals, reduce dry-run outages in APAC and EU, and preserve flexibility to swap SKUs between clusters if prices/lead times change.

Context and assumptions:
- We expect a 30–45% increase in sustained token throughput year-over-year tied to product launches (chat + streaming).
- Current committed budget for Q4–Q1 procurement is $18M (capex + partial lease).
- Vendors: V1 (direct OEM regional), V2 (global distributor), V3 (refurb/secondary market broker).
- Lead-time volatility: OEM queues vary by region; we must plan for 6–20 week windows.
- Interchangeability: see SKU interchange matrix below — not all SKUs are drop-in for all inference pools.

High-level recommendation summary:
- Use 3 tranche lanes per SKU family: baseline (committed), opportunistic (market-priced), contingency (refurb/broker).
- Slice inbound deliveries across 6 warehouses/regions: US-W, US-E, EU-W, EU-C, AP-SE, AP-N.
- Reserve ~18% of budget for opportunistic captures and 6% for emergency broker buys.
- Implement SKU interchangeability tagging in inventory DB (tags: kv-cache-friendly, quant-friendly, long-context-optimized).

Current inventory snapshot (approx, 2024-09-01):
- H100-80GB: 420 units (US-W: 140, US-E: 120, EU-W: 80, AP-SE: 40, rest reserve)
- A100-80GB: 310 units (US-W: 90, US-E: 80, EU-W: 60, AP-SE: 40, EU-C: 40)
- L40-32GB: 120 units (edge clusters in AP and EU-C)
- RTX6000/other: 60 units (QA/ethos/bench)
- Average fleet utilization (last 30d): US-W 78%, US-E 72%, EU 89% (spikes), APAC 94% (sustained peak nights)

SKU interchangeability matrix (short):
- H100: best for long-context and high-throughput batching. Can replace A100 in most RL/optim workloads but requires kernel tuning.
- A100: general purpose; fastest procurement options via distributors.
- L40: cost-efficient for replicated-small-context streaming and for embedding generation at scale.
- Policy: avoid mixing H100 and A100 in same instance pool unless runtime supports per-request kernel switching.

Proposed tranche schedule (per SKU family):
1) Baseline tranche (committed, lowest price volatility):
   - Size: 30–40% of 12-month planned addition for that SKU
   - Order window: place at T0, delivery estimated 8–12 weeks (region-dependent)
   - Payment terms: 30% deposit, balance on delivery
2) Rolling replenishment tranche (predictable cadence):
   - Size: 30% of need, ordered in 8-week cadence (T+8, T+16, ...)
   - Aim: smooth arrivals to warehouses; split across two vendors where possible
3) Opportunistic tranche (price/lead-time arbitrage):
   - Size: 20% of need
   - Trigger: market discount >= 12% vs OEM list OR lead-time advantage > 6 weeks
   - Vendor: prefer V2 or V3 depending on warranty/return terms
4) Contingency tranche (emergency broker/refurb):
   - Size: 10%–20% (flexible)
   - Use only if regional utilization > 95% for >72h or SLO risk flagged

Lead-time and vendor heuristics (empirical):
- H100 via OEM (V1): US regions 8–12w, EU 10–16w, AP 12–20w depending on factory allocations.
- A100 via distributor (V2): US 6–10w, EU 8–12w, AP 10–14w.
- Refurb brokers (V3): 2–6w availability, warranty 6–12 months, pricing varies 30–60% of new list.
- Shipping and customs add 1–3w on top of lead time for EU-AP crossflows.

Warehouse slicing rationale and allocation rules:
- Goal: limit single-warehouse arrival concentration > 25% of incoming tranche for a given week.
- Primary hubs: US-W (SFO), EU-W (AMS), AP-SE (SG). Secondary: US-E (IAD), EU-C (FRA), AP-N (TYO).
- Slice each incoming PO into micro-shipments (3–6 packages) across 2–3 hubs when possible to mitigate transit delays and customs holdups.
- For high-value H100 shipments, favor direct-to-region OEM shipments to reduce broker tinkering.

Example order plan (Q4 start, target +900 units mix):
- H100 target add: +420 units over 12 months -> baseline order 140 (T0), rolling 140 (T+8/T+16), opportunistic 60, contingency 80.
- A100 target add: +300 units -> baseline 100, rolling 100, opportunistic 50, contingency 50.
- L40 target add: +180 units -> baseline 50, rolling 80, opportunistic 30, contingency 20.
- Warehouse distribution: default split 30/25/20/10/10/5 across primary/secondary hubs; adjust by region utilization curve.

Inventory handling & ops notes (ops-runbook items):
- On arrival: tag units with SKU/region/warehouse/date/vendor/serial in InventoryDB; auto-assign interchange-key.
- Quarantine window: 72h warm-up and perf-check for H100s (burn-in images).
- KMS keying: units destined for Private installs require pre-approved KMS mapping before shipment. Add 2–3d ops work to delivery pipeline.
- Redistribution: if EU utilization < 70% and AP > 90%, allow automated cross-region transfer for up to 25% of new arrivals (cost model calc required).

Risk register (short):
- Single-vendor OEM backlog spike -> increased lead to 16–20w (mitigation: larger opportunistic tranche commitment with distributor).
- Customs holdup in EU (seasonal) -> 2–3w delay: mitigation slice shipments and pre-clearance docs.
- Broker units with limited warranty -> increased failure rates: hold bigger contingency pool and maintain spare reserve units in US-W.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Approve reserve budget of 6% for broker/emergency purchases? (Finance decision, linked JIRA INFRA-4923).
- Should we standardize on 3 vendors per SKU family or add dynamic vendor scoring? (Product Ops wants vendor scoring; eng prefers narrow approved list).
- Routing policy: do we prefer cost-minimization (ship to low-cost hubs) or SLO-first (ship to high-util regions)? We need an executive tradeoff.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: finalize tranche calendar + vendor ROIs by 2024-09-30.
- Ravi: update InventoryDB schema to store interchange tags and warehouse-slice-id by 2024-10-07 (PR pending).
- Marta: run 6-week simulation of cross-region transfer costs and update ops playbook by 2024-10-21.
- Diego: draft vendor SLAs and extended-warranty negotiation points (V1/V2) by 2024-09-25.

Notes / friction points (freeform):
- Ops flagged that warehouse partner for EU-C lacks PCI/physical-seal capability for high-value crates; need alternate secondary partner.
- Finance prefers leasing to reduce capex exposure but procurement/legal note longer lead negotiation for lease terms.
- Suggest a small pilot: 40-unit H100 tranche via V2 direct-to-EU and 40-unit via V1 split across US+AP to empirically measure arrival variance.

References and links:
- Slack: #infra-procurement thread "H100 tranche windows" (pinned discussion 2024-09-01)
- JIRA: INFRA-4923 (budget approval)
- Confluence: FleetCapacity/TrancheStrategy (draft)

This doc is intentionally a working draft — please add comments inline or link suggested vendor contacts.
